rules.title: Apple one-year limited warranty
rules.window_note: One year from the day you bought it. Apple can check the date from the serial number, so you don't always need the receipt.
rules.what_you_get: Apple picks one: a free repair using real Apple parts, a swap for the same model, or your money back.
rules.how_to_claim: Book a free appointment at an Apple Store or an Apple Authorised Service Provider, or start a repair online. Mail-in repair is free too — Apple pays the shipping if you follow their instructions.
rules.script_hint: My Apple product has stopped working properly and it is still inside the one-year limited warranty. Please repair or replace it under warranty.

rules.title: Samsung one-year limited warranty
rules.window_note: One year (12 months) from when you bought it. Same length for phones, tablets, TVs, laptops and most home appliances.
rules.what_you_get: A free fix for a fault that was the factory's fault — Samsung pays for the part and the work.
rules.how_to_claim: Add the product to your Samsung account at samsung.com/us/support/register, open it under My Products, then press Request Service. On a Galaxy phone you can also do it in the Samsung Members app.
rules.script_hint: My Samsung product has a fault that isn't from damage or misuse, and it's still inside the one-year limited warranty. Please book a warranty repair.

rules.title: Google one-year hardware warranty
rules.window_note: One year from the day you bought it new. Refurbished Google devices only get 90 days. Damage or decline that comes from normal everyday use is specifically not covered.
rules.what_you_get: Google either repairs it, sends you a replacement device, or refunds you.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to g.co/warrantyclaim (or store.google.com/repair). Have your serial number or IMEI and your proof of purchase ready. You can pick a walk-in repair shop or post it in.
rules.script_hint: My Google device is faulty and it's still inside the one-year limited warranty. Here's my serial number and proof of purchase — please repair or replace it.

rules.title: Dell limited hardware warranty
rules.window_note: The exact length is printed on your invoice, receipt or packing slip. Most home laptops come with 1 year; some come with 2, 3 or more. The battery always gets at least 1 year even if the laptop's cover is longer.
rules.what_you_get: Dell fixes the broken part for free — they post you a part, take the machine in, or send a technician to your home if your plan includes that.
rules.how_to_claim: Call Dell hardware warranty support with your Service Tag ready, or start it at dell.com/support. They will do a remote check first, then arrange the fix.
rules.script_hint: My Dell is faulty and it's still inside the limited hardware warranty. My Service Tag is ___ — please arrange a warranty repair.

rules.title: LG TV one-year warranty
rules.window_note: One year from the day you bought it. You need the original sales receipt showing the TV and the date.
rules.what_you_get: LG repairs or replaces the TV. Both the parts inside and the labour are free.
rules.how_to_claim: Book a repair on LG's support site or ring LG customer service. Have the model number, serial number and receipt to hand.
rules.script_hint: My LG TV failed on its own, not from damage, and it's under a year old. Please book a warranty repair — I have the receipt.

rules.title: Bose one-year limited warranty
rules.window_note: One year from the day you bought it, for headphones, earbuds and speakers. Bose aviation headsets and passive (non-powered) speakers get five years instead.
rules.what_you_get: Bose repairs it, swaps it for an equal new or refurbished one, or gives some or all of your money back.
rules.how_to_claim: Contact Bose support and ask for warranty service — they'll send return instructions. Keep your receipt: Bose can ask for proof of purchase, and gear bought from unauthorised sellers isn't covered.
rules.script_hint: My Bose product has a fault in the materials or workmanship and it's still inside the one-year limited warranty. Please arrange repair or replacement.

rules.title: Whirlpool one-year appliance warranty
rules.window_note: One year from the day you bought it. Keep the receipt — Whirlpool needs proof of the purchase date.
rules.what_you_get: Whirlpool pays for the replacement parts AND the repair person's time to fix a factory fault. If they can't fix it they may swap the appliance.
rules.how_to_claim: Contact Whirlpool and ask for warranty service. The repair must be done by a Whirlpool-approved service company, and you'll need your model number, serial number, receipt and a clear description of the problem.
rules.script_hint: My Whirlpool appliance has a fault in the materials or workmanship and it's under a year old. Please send a Whirlpool-designated servicer under the one-year limited warranty.

rules.title: GE Appliances one-year warranty
rules.window_note: One year from the day you bought it. Some single parts (like a sealed cooling system) are covered longer — check the warranty page in your manual.
rules.what_you_get: GE replaces any part that fails because of a factory fault, and pays for the labour and the home visit too.
rules.how_to_claim: Book service online at geappliances.com or ring GE Appliance Service. Have your model and serial number ready.
rules.script_hint: My GE appliance has failed because of a defect in materials or workmanship and it's under a year old. Please schedule warranty service.

rules.title: KitchenAid stand mixer one-year replacement
rules.window_note: One year from the day it was delivered. Most other KitchenAid appliances are also about one year; dishwashers can start at two.
rules.what_you_get: A hassle-free replacement — KitchenAid sends you another mixer rather than making you get it repaired.
rules.how_to_claim: Ring KitchenAid customer service with your model number, serial number, a clear description of the problem and your proof of purchase (shop name and date).
rules.script_hint: My KitchenAid stand mixer stopped working and it's under a year old. The warranty says hassle-free replacement — please send a replacement.

rules.title: Vitamix full warranty (5, 7 or 10 years)
rules.window_note: Depends on the model: 5, 7 or 10 years from purchase. Check which one your blender came with — the 7-year is the most common on classic models.
rules.what_you_get: A free fix or a free replacement part, including the labour AND the postage both ways. It's a full warranty, not a part-payment one.
rules.how_to_claim: Ring Vitamix customer service. Registering your machine helps but the warranty still applies if you didn't.
rules.script_hint: My Vitamix isn't working right and it's still inside the full warranty period. Please arrange a repair or replacement part at no cost, including shipping.

rules.title: DeWalt 3-year power tool warranty
rules.window_note: Three years from purchase for most tools (a few get seven). On top of that you get one year of free servicing and a 90-day money-back guarantee.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement for a factory fault. In the first year DeWalt will also service and tune the tool for free. In the first 90 days you can just get your money back.
rules.how_to_claim: Take the tool to a DeWalt service centre or the shop you bought it from, or file a request online. Bring proof of purchase showing when and where you bought it.
rules.script_hint: My DeWalt tool has failed from a defect in materials or workmanship, and it's inside the 3-year limited warranty. Please repair or replace it.

rules.title: Milwaukee 5-year power tool warranty
rules.window_note: Five years from purchase for most cordless power tools. Batteries get less: usually three years. Hand tools have a limited lifetime warranty. You do NOT need to have registered the tool.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement for a fault in the materials or workmanship.
rules.how_to_claim: Send or take the tool to a Milwaukee factory service centre or authorised service station with a copy of your receipt. No receipt? They can use the date stamped on the tool instead.
rules.script_hint: My Milwaukee tool has failed from a defect in material or workmanship and it's inside the 5-year warranty. Please repair or replace it — no registration is needed.

rules.title: Le Creuset lifetime warranty on enameled cast iron
rules.window_note: Lasts as long as you own it, starting the day you bought it. Only for home cooking, and only for enameled cast iron — non-stick pans and non-cast-iron bits aren't covered. Only counts for the person who bought it.
rules.what_you_get: Le Creuset makes good a pot or pan that was faulty in its materials or workmanship.
rules.how_to_claim: Ring Le Creuset consumer services and describe the fault. You pay the postage to send the item in; they don't cover that part.
rules.script_hint: My Le Creuset enameled cast iron pot has a defect in materials or workmanship. I'm the original owner and I'd like to claim under the Lifetime Limited Warranty.

rules.title: YETI 5-year warranty
rules.window_note: Five years from purchase for hard coolers, Rambler drinkware, LoadOut gear and chairs. Three years for soft coolers and most bags. Only counts if you bought from YETI or an approved shop.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement product or part. If your exact one has been discontinued they send a similar one.
rules.how_to_claim: Fill in the online warranty claim form. If it's approved YETI sends you a prepaid shipping label — don't post it before you get that.
rules.script_hint: My YETI product has a defect in workmanship or materials and it's inside the warranty period. I used it as intended and followed the care instructions — please replace it.

rules.title: Stanley lifetime warranty on stainless steel bottles and cups
rules.window_note: Lasts the life of the product, with no time limit. It covers the stainless steel body — but not the lids, seals or straws, and not scratches and dents from normal use. Importantly it DOES cover a bottle that stops keeping drinks hot or cold.
rules.what_you_get: A repair or a free replacement bottle, cup or food jar of a similar current model.
rules.how_to_claim: Fill in Stanley's online warranty claim form with photos. They may ask for proof of purchase or for the item back.
rules.script_hint: My Stanley bottle no longer keeps drinks hot or cold. The lifetime warranty covers loss of thermal performance — please replace it.

rules.title: Osprey All Mighty Guarantee
rules.window_note: Any age, any reason. Osprey say it plainly: whether the bag was made in 1974 or yesterday. A few products are the exception — Poco child carriers (7 years), Soelden/Sopris Pro and Raptor Pro (5 years).
rules.what_you_get: A free repair of any damage or defect, for any reason — even damage you caused. If they can't fix it, they replace it. Cosmetic marks aren't covered.
rules.how_to_claim: Fill in the repair form on Osprey's All Mighty Guarantee page, write the AMG number they give you on the box, and post it to them. You pay postage to them; they pay the repair and the return. Turnaround is about 6 to 10 weeks. Don't send it dirty or mouldy — they'll refuse it.
rules.script_hint: I'd like to use the All Mighty Guarantee. My Osprey pack has this damage: ___ . Please repair it, or replace it if it can't be repaired.

rules.title: Patagonia Ironclad Guarantee
rules.window_note: No time limit is stated — the promise covers everything they make. But there's a catch worth knowing: damage from ordinary wear and tear gets repaired for a fair charge, not free. For repairs, contact the Worn Wear team — they also publish free step-by-step guides if you would rather fix it yourself.
rules.what_you_get: If the item doesn't perform the way it should: a repair, a replacement or a refund. If it's just worn out from use: a repair at a reasonable price.
rules.how_to_claim: Take it back to the shop you bought it from, or start a mail-in repair on patagonia.com. Repairs take up to about 10 weeks.
rules.script_hint: This Patagonia item hasn't performed the way it should. Under the Ironclad Guarantee I'd like a repair, replacement or refund.

rules.title: Nike two-year flaw warranty
rules.window_note: Two years from the MANUFACTURE date printed on the tag inside the shoe or garment — not from the day you bought it. So a pair that sat in a shop for a year only has a year left. Separately, anything bought from Nike can be returned for any reason within 60 days.
rules.what_you_get: Nike inspects the item, and if there's a real material or workmanship flaw they email you a Nike gift card for it and recycle the faulty one.
rules.how_to_claim: If you bought it from another shop, take it back there first. If they send you back to Nike, file a claim at nikeclaims.com. You'll need the place and date of purchase, the manufacture date on the tag, the 9-digit style code and the receipt amount.
rules.script_hint: These Nike shoes have a material or workmanship flaw and the manufacture date on the tag is less than two years ago. The retailer sent me back to Nike — please inspect them.

rules.title: Timex one-year watch warranty
rules.window_note: One year from the day you bought it. Some Timex watches come with a longer limited lifetime warranty on the movement — check what came in your box. Second-hand watches aren't covered.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair of a making fault (you still pay a small handling fee). If it can't be fixed because the parts don't exist any more, they may swap it for the same or a similar model.
rules.how_to_claim: Start a repair at the online Timex Watch Repair Shop, or send the watch to an authorised Timex repair centre with the receipt showing the date, item and shop. Never post the original box.
rules.script_hint: My Timex has a manufacturing defect and it's less than a year old. I've attached my receipt — please repair it under the warranty.

rules.title: L.L.Bean guarantee
rules.window_note: One year to return anything for any reason if you're not happy with it. After that year there's no hard cut-off, but they'll only look at items that are actually faulty in their materials or craftsmanship — not things you simply wore out.
rules.what_you_get: A refund within the first year. After a year, they consider faulty items case by case.
rules.how_to_claim: Return it to an L.L.Bean shop or post it back with a Return and Exchange Form. Gift returns get store credit if you have a gift receipt.
rules.script_hint: This L.L.Bean item is defective in its materials or craftsmanship. Your guarantee says you'll consider defective items after the one-year window — please take a look.

rules.title: Visa Signature / Visa Infinite purchase security (US)
rules.window_note: Covers the first 90 days after you buy something. If it is stolen or broken in that time, you then have 60 days from the day it happened to phone in, and 90 days to send the paperwork. Most people find out too late. It even covers the deductible your home insurance would make you pay. If you have home or renters insurance, you have to file with them first and send Visa a copy of what they paid.
rules.what_you_get: Your item repaired, replaced, or your money back if it is stolen or accidentally damaged in the first 90 days. Up to $10,000 for one claim and $50,000 total per cardholder.
rules.how_to_claim: Call the benefits number on the back of your card within 60 days of the theft or damage (Visa's guides list 1-888-221-3289), or start it at cardbenefitservices.com. If it was stolen, file a police report first. Send back the signed form, the receipt and your statement within 90 days.
rules.script_hint: I'd like to open a Purchase Security claim. My [item] was [stolen / damaged] on [date], which was within 90 days of buying it on this Visa card.

rules.title: Mastercard purchase assurance / damage and theft protection (US)
rules.window_note: Covers damage or theft in the first 90 days after you buy. You then have 60 days from the day it happened to report it, and 180 days to send documents. This one usually comes with World and World Elite cards, not basic ones.
rules.what_you_get: Repair, replacement, or money back if a new item is broken or stolen within 90 days. Commonly $1,000 per incident and $25,000 a year, though the cap varies by card.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to mycardbenefits.com or call the benefits number in your card's Guide to Benefits (Capital One's World Elite guide lists 1-877-288-6784) within 60 days of the loss. Get a police report if it was stolen. Then send the receipt, statement, photos or a repair estimate within 180 days.
rules.script_hint: I want to file a Purchase Assurance claim. My [item] was [damaged / stolen] on [date], less than 90 days after I bought it with this Mastercard.

rules.title: American Express extended warranty (US)
rules.window_note: Amex adds up to one extra year on any maker's warranty of 5 years or less. That 5-year limit is much more generous than Visa's 3 years or a basic Mastercard's 1 year. But you only get 30 days from the day it breaks to tell Amex, and 60 days to send proof. Amex used to add 2 years; it was cut to 1 year for purchases from 1 October 2020.
rules.what_you_get: The same repair or replacement the maker's warranty would have covered, for a year longer. Up to $10,000 per item and $50,000 per card per calendar year.
rules.how_to_claim: File online at americanexpress.com/onlineclaim or call 1-800-228-6855 within 30 days of the item breaking. Then send the itemised receipt, a copy of the maker's warranty, and a photo or repair estimate within 60 days.
rules.script_hint: I'm filing an Extended Warranty claim. My [item] stopped working on [date], after the manufacturer's warranty ended, and I charged the whole purchase to my American Express card.

rules.title: American Express purchase protection (US)
rules.window_note: Covers the first 90 days after you buy. Amex is one of the few that also covers an item you simply lost, not just stolen or broken. You must tell Amex within 30 days of it happening and send proof within 60 days. Some entry-level Amex cards cap it at $1,000 per incident instead, so check yours.
rules.what_you_get: Repair, replacement or a refund if a new item is accidentally damaged, stolen, or lost within 90 days of buying it. Up to $10,000 per item and $50,000 per card per calendar year (only $500 if the cause was a natural disaster).
rules.how_to_claim: File at americanexpress.com/onlineclaim or call 1-800-228-6855 within 30 days of the damage, theft or loss. Report theft to the police before you call. Then send the itemised receipt, photos or a repair estimate, and any home insurance details within 60 days.
rules.script_hint: I'm filing a Purchase Protection claim. My [item] was [damaged / stolen / lost] on [date], within 90 days of buying it on my Amex.

rules.title: Chase purchase protection (US)
rules.window_note: Chase gives 120 days after you buy, longer than the usual 90. New York residents get 90 days. Once something happens you have 90 days to report it and 120 days to send documents. Sapphire Preferred and Freedom pay up to $500 an item, Sapphire Reserve up to $10,000 an item. For theft, file a police report first.
rules.what_you_get: Repair, replacement or money back if a new item is stolen, damaged, or accidentally lost within 120 days of buying it. The cap depends on the card, often $500 or $10,000 per claim.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to chasecardbenefits.com or call the number on the back of your Chase card within 90 days of the theft or damage. Send everything they ask for within 120 days.
rules.script_hint: I'd like to file a Purchase Protection claim. My [item] was [damaged / stolen] on [date], within 120 days of buying it with my Chase card.

rules.title: Chase extended warranty protection (US)
rules.window_note: Adds one extra year, but only on maker's warranties of 3 years or less, so cover stops at 4 years from the purchase date. You have 90 days from the day it broke to phone and 120 days to send documents. Chase adds one extra year on top of the maker's warranty on Sapphire, Freedom and Ink cards.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement for a year after the maker's warranty ends. Up to $10,000 per item and $50,000 per account.
rules.how_to_claim: Call the benefits number on the back of your Chase card, or use chasecardbenefits.com, within 90 days of the item failing. Send your statement, the itemised receipt, the maker's warranty and a repair estimate within 120 days.
rules.script_hint: I'd like to file an Extended Warranty Protection claim. My [item] failed on [date], after its manufacturer's warranty ended, and I paid for it with my Chase card.

rules.title: Visa purchase security (Canada)
rules.window_note: Covers 90 days from the purchase date, and Canadian Visa cover is wider than the US version because it includes loss and fire, not just theft and damage. The catch is a short reporting window: Scotiabank's certificate says you must phone no later than 45 days after the loss.
rules.what_you_get: Your item repaired, replaced, or your money back if it is lost, stolen, damaged, or burned in the first 90 days. Up to $10,000 per claim.
rules.how_to_claim: Phone the insurer named in your card's certificate of insurance before you fix or replace anything, and no later than 45 days after the loss (Scotiabank Visa Infinite cards use Elite Insurance at 1-800-665-3088). Report theft to the police first. Keep the original receipt, your charge slip, and your statement.
rules.script_hint: I'm reporting a Purchase Security claim. My [item] was [lost / stolen / damaged] on [date], within 90 days of buying it on my Visa card, and I have not had it repaired yet.

rules.title: Visa extended warranty (Canada)
rules.window_note: Doubles the maker's warranty, up to one extra year. Two traps: if the maker's warranty is 5 years or longer you must register the item with the insurer inside the first year of owning it or you get nothing, and you must phone before any repair work starts.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair for as long again as the maker's warranty lasted, up to one extra year. Up to $10,000 per claim.
rules.how_to_claim: Call the insurer listed in your card's certificate of insurance before you have anything repaired, within 45 days of the breakdown (Scotiabank Visa Infinite uses Elite Insurance, 1-800-665-3088). Send the original store receipt, your charge slip or statement, the maker's warranty, and a letter describing the fault with the brand, model and serial number.
rules.script_hint: I'm making an Extended Warranty claim on my Visa card. My [item] failed on [date] and I have not started any repairs yet, as the certificate requires.

rules.title: American Express Buyer's Assurance extended warranty (Canada)
rules.window_note: Doubles the maker's warranty by up to one extra year, on warranties of 5 years or less. You must charge the whole purchase to the card. Report within 45 days of the breakdown and send documents within 60 days. If the manufacturer goes bankrupt, the extra year starts from the bankruptcy date instead. They may ask you to get a repair estimate.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair, rebuild, replacement or cash back for the same faults the maker's warranty covered, for up to one extra year. Up to $10,000 per item and $25,000 per cardmember per policy year.
rules.how_to_claim: Call 1-800-243-0198 (free from Canada and the US) or go to info.submitclaims.client.insure within 45 days of the item failing. Send the original sales receipt, your Amex statement, and the maker's warranty within 60 days.
rules.script_hint: I'm reporting a Buyer's Assurance claim. My [item] stopped working on [date], after the manufacturer's warranty ended, and the full purchase was charged to my Amex card.

rules.title: American Express Purchase Protection Plan (Canada)
rules.window_note: Covers 90 days from the purchase date, and unlike the US version even a part payment on the card counts. But this has the tightest deadline of any card benefit here: you must phone within 48 hours of the theft or damage. Written notice should follow within 45 days and all documents within 90 days.
rules.what_you_get: Your item replaced, repaired, or the amount you put on the card refunded, if it is stolen or physically damaged within 90 days. Commonly $1,000 per incident, with higher caps on premium Amex cards.
rules.how_to_claim: Call 1-800-243-0198 within 48 hours of the theft or damage, or go to info.submitclaims.client.insure. Get a police report for theft. Send the purchase receipt, your statement, photos of the damage or a repair estimate, and your home insurance deductible details within 90 days.
rules.script_hint: I'm reporting a Purchase Protection Plan claim within the 48-hour window. My [item] was [stolen / damaged] on [date], within 90 days of buying it with my Amex.

rules.title: Mastercard purchase security and extended warranty (Canada)
rules.window_note: Two separate benefits on one certificate. Purchase security covers loss, theft or damage for 90 days after you buy. Extended warranty doubles the maker's warranty by up to one extra year, on warranties of 5 years or less. Report either one within 90 days of it happening, and return the claim form within 30 days of getting it.
rules.what_you_get: A repair, a replacement, or your money back. Purchase security pays up to $10,000 per claim; extended warranty gives the same free repairs the maker's warranty would have.
rules.how_to_claim: Call the claims number in your card's certificate of insurance within 90 days (Canadian Tire's Triangle World Elite Mastercard uses 1-800-797-8389). Report theft to the police first. Keep the original receipt and the maker's warranty, and return the completed claim form within 30 days of receiving it.
rules.script_hint: I'm reporting a claim under my Mastercard's purchase security and extended warranty insurance. My [item] was [stolen / damaged / failed] on [date].

rules.title: Whirlpool broken-wire fridge settlement (Whirlpool, Maytag, KitchenAid, JennAir)
rules.window_note: Covers side-by-side fridges made by Whirlpool from 2018 to 2021, for breakdowns from year 2 up to year 7 after you bought it. If it already broke, you must file by 2 November 2026. If it breaks after 5 May 2026, you instead have 90 days from the day you notice it. (they pay the fitting too if it broke in years 2 to 4) Have your receipt or repair bill handy if you have one. Ring Whirlpool on 1-844-667-2929, or email refset2026@Whirlpool.com, within 90 days of noticing it. Do this BEFORE you pay anyone to fix it, or you lose the free repair.
rules.what_you_get: A free new freezer door (with free labour in the earlier years), or cash instead — 30% to 50% of what you paid for the fridge. If you already paid someone to fix it, you get 35% to 75% of that repair bill back. If you gave up and bought a new fridge, you get 25% to 50% of the old one's price back.
rules.how_to_claim: Find the model and serial number inside your fridge, then fill in the claim form at RefrigeratorSettlement.com before 2 November 2026. If it breaks after 5 May 2026, phone Whirlpool on 1-844-667-2929 within 90 days instead of filing.
rules.script_hint: My side-by-side fridge has the broken wire problem in the freezer door — the ice maker and water dispenser stopped working. I am a class member in the Costa v. Whirlpool settlement and I want the free replacement door.

rules.title: Hyundai and Kia airbag control unit settlement
rules.window_note: You had to own or lease the car on 14 April 2025. It does not matter when you bought it — what matters is filing before 8 April 2027. Covers certain Sonata, Sonata Hybrid, Kona, Kona N, Veloster, Forte, Forte Koup, Optima, Optima Hybrid and Sedona models from 2010 to 2023. You can claim even if you sold the car or it was a lease.
rules.what_you_get: Up to $350 cash if your car was recalled, or up to $150 if it was not. Plus your money back for a rental car, towing, childcare or lost pay while the recall was being fixed. Cars that got the new part also get a 10-year warranty on it.
rules.how_to_claim: Type your VIN into the checker at acusettlement.com to see if your car counts, then file the claim form on that same site before 8 April 2027.
rules.script_hint: I owned or leased a Hyundai or Kia listed in the ZF-TRW airbag control unit settlement on 14 April 2025, and I am claiming the residual payment plus my out-of-pocket recall costs.

rules.title: BMW shark-fin antenna leak settlement
rules.window_note: Covers 2019 and 2020 BMW X3, X4, X5, X6 and X7. Money back for repairs you already paid for must be claimed by 27 August 2026. The stretched warranty keeps covering future leaks even if you never file a claim.
rules.what_you_get: Money back for what you already paid to fix the leaking shark-fin antenna, plus BMW's new-car warranty stretched out to keep covering this leak in future.
rules.how_to_claim: File the claim form at sharkfinsettlement.com with your repair receipt before 27 August 2026, or call the administrator on 833-447-8559.
rules.script_hint: My 2019 or 2020 BMW X-series had water leaking in through the shark-fin antenna. I am a class member in Craft v. BMW of North America and I am claiming my repair costs back.

rules.title: Hyundai engine settlement 15-year extended warranty
rules.window_note: 15 years or 150,000 miles from when the car was first sold, whichever comes first. There is no form and no deadline for this part — but you must have had the free KSDS software update done at a dealer before the engine failed. Covers Sonata Hybrid, Santa Fe, Tucson, Elantra, Elantra GT, Elantra Coupe and Veloster over various years from 2010 to 2021.
rules.what_you_get: A free engine repair or replacement (short block or long block) when the connecting rod bearing fails. It transfers to whoever owns the car next.
rules.how_to_claim: Take the car to a Hyundai dealer and ask them to open a warranty claim under the Engine Litigation II settlement extended warranty. No claim form is needed for this.
rules.script_hint: My engine failed from connecting rod bearing damage. My car is covered by the 15-year, 150,000-mile extended powertrain warranty from the In re: Hyundai and Kia Engine Litigation II settlement, and my KSDS update was already done.

rules.title: Kia engine settlement 15-year extended warranty
rules.window_note: 15 years or 150,000 miles from when the car was first sold, whichever comes first. No form and no deadline for the free repair itself, as long as the free KSDS update was done. Separately, if your engine failed after 7 June 2023 and you paid costs, you have 90 days from that cost to file for money back.
rules.what_you_get: A free engine repair or replacement when the connecting rod bearing wears out. If you paid out of pocket, you can also claim back towing, transport and sometimes food and lodging.
rules.how_to_claim: Check your VIN at kiaengineclasssettlement.com or ring 1-800-944-1025. For the free repair, just take it to a Kia dealer — no form. For money back on a failure after 7 June 2023, file the claim form within 90 days of paying.
rules.script_hint: My Kia engine failed from connecting rod bearing wear. It is covered by the 15-year, 150,000-mile extended powertrain warranty from the In re: Hyundai and Kia Engine Litigation II settlement, and my KSDS update was done.

rules.title: Apple iPhone 14 Plus rear camera service programme
rules.window_note: Only the iPhone 14 Plus, made between 10 April 2023 and 28 April 2024. Free for three years from when it was first sold.
rules.what_you_get: A free rear camera repair. If you already paid to have that camera fixed, you can ask Apple for that money back.
rules.how_to_claim: Put your serial number into the checker on Apple's programme page, then book an Apple Store appointment, use an Authorised Service Provider, or ask Apple Support for post-in repair. If you already paid, use the refund link on that same page.
rules.script_hint: My iPhone 14 Plus rear camera shows no preview. Please check my serial number against the iPhone 14 Plus Service Program for Rear Camera Issue.

rules.title: Apple 15-inch MacBook Pro battery recall
rules.window_note: Only the MacBook Pro (Retina, 15-inch, Mid 2015), sold mostly between September 2015 and February 2017. This is a fire-safety recall, so Apple has not set a cut-off date — it is still listed on Apple's live programme page.
rules.what_you_get: A free new battery, because the old one can overheat and start a fire. Stop using the laptop until it is swapped.
rules.how_to_claim: Check that About This Mac says MacBook Pro (Retina, 15-inch, Mid 2015), put the serial number into Apple's checker, then book an Apple Store or Authorised Service Provider appointment. Back up your files first.
rules.script_hint: I have a 15-inch MacBook Pro Mid 2015. Please check my serial number against the 15-inch MacBook Pro Battery Recall Program — I need the free battery replacement.

rules.title: Apple three-prong wall plug adapter recall
rules.window_note: The white three-prong plug adapter shipped from 2003 to 2010 with Macs, iPhones and iPads, and inside the Apple World Travel Adapter Kit. Mainly the UK, Singapore and Hong Kong style plug. No cut-off date. Adapters for Europe, Australia, New Zealand, Korea, Argentina and Brazil are covered by a separate Apple recall.
rules.what_you_get: A free swap for a new, safe plug adapter. The old one can break apart and give you an electric shock.
rules.how_to_claim: Check whether the inside slot is plain white with no letters — that is the affected one. Take it, plus the serial number of your Apple device, to an Apple Store or Authorised Service Provider for a free exchange.
rules.script_hint: I have one of the white three-prong wall plug adapters covered by Apple's recall programme, and I would like the free exchange.

rules.title: Free fix for any open car safety recall
rules.window_note: The fix is free as long as the recall was announced within 15 years of the car first being sold. Once your car is covered, there is no deadline to actually get the work done. It is against the law for a dealer to charge you for it.
rules.what_you_get: A free fix at any franchised dealer — parts and labour included. Sometimes the maker replaces the part, refunds you, or buys the car back instead.
rules.how_to_claim: Type your number plate or VIN into the free checker at nhtsa.gov/recalls. If anything comes up, ring your local main dealer for that brand and book it in. Check twice a year, because new recalls get added.
rules.script_hint: My VIN shows an open safety recall. Federal law says the recall repair is free, so please book me in at no charge.

rules.title: Takata exploding airbag recall
rules.window_note: About 67 million airbags across dozens of car brands are recalled. No deadline and no charge. Certain 2001-2003 Hondas and Acuras are treated as so dangerous that you should only drive them to the dealer and nowhere else.
rules.what_you_get: A free airbag replacement. The old airbag can explode when it goes off and fire metal shrapnel at whoever is sitting there.
rules.how_to_claim: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls, then ring your local dealer and book the free repair. If you have a 2001-2003 Honda or Acura, ring Honda on 844-758-9245 straight away.
rules.script_hint: My car is on the Takata airbag recall list. I need the free replacement inflator booked in as soon as possible.

rules.title: Free fix, swap or refund on any recalled product
rules.window_note: There is usually no end date on a product recall. You can still claim years after it was announced, and you do not need to have kept the receipt. Have the model number handy (on a label on the product) because recalls often cover only certain model or date codes. Even if the recall was announced years ago, you can still claim the remedy if your item was never fixed or replaced. Strollers, bikes, e-bike and scooter batteries, camping stoves and power stations all get recalled often, and the fix costs you nothing.
rules.what_you_get: A free fix, a free replacement, or your full money back — the company chooses which one it offers. Postage is usually covered too.
rules.how_to_claim: Search your product at cpsc.gov/Recalls. Follow the instructions in the recall notice — normally a free phone number or a sign-up page. If the company does not reply within about a week, ring CPSC on (800) 638-2772 or report it at SaferProducts.gov.
rules.script_hint: My [product and model number] is on the CPSC recall list. I would like the remedy you announced — the free repair, replacement or refund. I no longer have the receipt, which your recall notice says is fine.

rules.title: California secret warranty law — refund for a repair you paid for
rules.window_note: California only. You have two years from the day you paid the repair bill to ask for that money back. Carmakers must tell owners about these quiet fix-it programmes within 90 days of starting one.
rules.what_you_get: Your money back for a repair you paid for yourself, if the carmaker had a quiet free-fix programme for that exact fault and did not tell you about it.
rules.how_to_claim: Ask the dealer or the carmaker in writing whether there is a warranty adjustment programme or service bulletin covering your fault. If there is, and you paid for that repair within the last two years, ask for a refund. They must tell you yes or no within 21 working days, and give reasons if they say no.
rules.script_hint: Under California Civil Code section 1795.92, if there is an adjustment programme covering this condition, I am requesting reimbursement for the repair I paid for on [date].

rules.title: US: outside parts and outside repairs can't void your warranty
rules.window_note: This works for as long as the product's warranty is still running. There's no extra deadline of its own. They can only refuse if that outside part or repair is what actually caused the damage. A maker can only require their own brand if they hand it to you free. Ask them to prove that supply caused this fault — that proof is on them, not you.
rules.what_you_get: The company still has to give you the free repair or replacement it promised, even though you used a part that wasn't theirs or took it to a local shop. Those "warranty void if this sticker is removed" stickers don't count either — the FTC has fined companies for using them.
rules.how_to_claim: Call the maker's warranty line and ask for the repair. If they say the warranty is void because of the part you used or the shop you went to, say the sentence below. If they still refuse, report them at reportfraud.ftc.gov — the FTC has already made Weber, Harley-Davidson and Westinghouse change their warranties over exactly this.
rules.script_hint: Federal law says you can't void my warranty because I used a non-brand part or an independent repair shop. That's the anti-tying rule in the Magnuson-Moss Warranty Act, 15 U.S.C. 2302(c). Please book the repair.

rules.title: US: if you sue over a warranty and win, they pay your lawyer
rules.window_note: No deadline of its own — it rides along with whatever warranty claim you're already making. Small claims court is cheap and you don't need a lawyer give them a date to reply by.
rules.what_you_get: Your fix or refund, plus the court can order the company to pay your legal costs and your lawyer's actual hours. That's why consumer lawyers take these cases with no money up front, and why naming this rule in a letter often ends the stalling on its own.
rules.how_to_claim: Put it in your written complaint before you sue. If you do go ahead, look for a lawyer who handles Magnuson-Moss cases — most work on the fees the other side has to pay.
rules.script_hint: Under the Magnuson-Moss Warranty Act, 15 U.S.C. 2310(d)(2), if I have to sue over this warranty and I win, the court can order you to pay my attorney's fees. I'd rather you just fixed it.

rules.title: Quebec: "we don't make that part anymore" is no longer allowed
rules.window_note: In force since 5 October 2025. There's no purchase-date cutoff for asking — the duty sits on the seller and the maker to keep parts, repair services and repair instructions available for a reasonable time at a reasonable price.
rules.what_you_get: The spare part, someone to do the repair, and the information needed to do it — instead of being told the part is discontinued. If they can't supply it, that's their problem to fix, not yours to eat.
rules.how_to_claim: Ask the merchant or the manufacturer in writing for the part or the repair, and name the warranty of availability of replacement parts and repair services. If they refuse or quote a silly price, call the OPC.
rules.script_hint: Quebec's Consumer Protection Act includes a legal warranty that replacement parts, repair services and the information needed to repair goods stay available for a reasonable time at a reasonable price. Please supply the part or the repair.

rules.title: Quebec: a fixed free-repair clock on appliances and electronics
rules.window_note: Starts 5 October 2026. After that: 6 years on stoves, fridges, freezers, air conditioners and heat pumps; 5 years on dishwashers, washing machines and dryers; 4 years on TVs; 3 years on computers, tablets, phones and game consoles — counted from delivery.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair with no argument about what "reasonable" means. Inside those years the maker or the seller simply has to fix it at no cost to you. This sits on top of the older durability warranty, it doesn't replace it.
rules.how_to_claim: Find your product in the list above, work out whether you're still inside the years, then contact the maker or the shop and ask for the free repair under the warranty of good working order.
rules.script_hint: This is covered by Quebec's legal warranty of good working order, which runs several years from delivery for this kind of product. It stopped working inside that period, so I'm asking for a free repair.

rules.title: UK: the shop stays on the hook for up to six years
rules.window_note: Six years in England, Wales and Northern Ireland; five in Scotland. In the first six months the shop has to prove the fault wasn't there when you bought it — after that it's on you to show it was. Careful: six years isn't a promise the product lasts six years, it's how long you have to bring the claim about a fault that shouldn't have happened. After the first 6 months you do have to show the fault was there from the start — usually with an independent repairer's report. Get an independent repairer to write down what failed and why it was a manufacturing problem. In the first 30 days you can simply reject the item and get your money back. A £900 washing machine that dies at year three is a fair argument; a £30 kettle is not.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement from the retailer, long after the brand's one-year guarantee ran out. If the repair fails or drags on, a price reduction or a refund — and in the first six months they can't knock money off for the use you already had.
rules.how_to_claim: Write to the retailer, not the brand. Say the goods weren't of satisfactory quality under section 9 of the Consumer Rights Act 2015, and that satisfactory quality expressly includes durability. If they refuse, the small claims track is designed for this and doesn't need a lawyer.
rules.script_hint: Under section 9 of the Consumer Rights Act 2015 these goods had to be of satisfactory quality, and that includes durability. A product at this price should not have failed after this long. As the retailer, I'm asking you for a free repair or replacement.

rules.title: EU: two free years from the shop, whatever the brand's card says
rules.window_note: At least two years everywhere in the EU, counted from the day it was delivered. In the first year the seller has to prove the fault wasn't there from the start; some countries stretch that to two years, and some countries give more than two years overall — check your own country's page on the EU's Your Europe site. A few countries also expect you to tell the seller within two months of spotting the fault, so don't sit on it. That includes paying to take the old one back, and taking out and refitting anything that was installed. Second-hand goods from a trader are covered too. If the manufacturer tells you that you're out of warranty, stop there and go back to the shop instead.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement from the seller. If they can't do it properly, in a reasonable time, and without a lot of hassle for you, then a price cut or your money back. It costs nothing and the brand's own "commercial guarantee" sits on top of it and can never shrink it.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to the seller you bought from, not the manufacturer — even if the brand's own guarantee has expired. If you bought from a shop in another EU country, your national European Consumer Centre will chase it for you for free, in your language.
rules.script_hint: Under the EU legal guarantee (Directive 2019/771) you as the seller are liable for a lack of conformity that appears within two years of delivery. I'm asking for a free repair or replacement.

rules.title: EU: makers must repair it, even after the guarantee has ended
rules.window_note: Applies from 31 July 2026, the date every EU country had to have it in their own law — a few were still catching up, so it may not have landed in yours yet. It covers washing machines, dishwashers, fridges, vacuum cleaners, phones, tablets, screens and e-bikes, and it works years after the guarantee is gone.
rules.what_you_get: Two separate things. One: the maker has to repair these products when you ask, at a reasonable price and in a reasonable time, even out of guarantee. Two: if you choose repair instead of replacement while still inside the legal guarantee, you get an extra 12 months of guarantee added on — once.
rules.how_to_claim: Ask the manufacturer directly for the repair and ask for the European Repair Information Form, which puts the price and conditions in writing before you commit to anything. Your national European Consumer Centre can chase it if they stall.
rules.script_hint: Directive (EU) 2024/1799 requires you as the producer to repair this product on request at a reasonable price. Please send me a European Repair Information Form with the price and how long it will take.

rules.title: EU: phone and tablet parts must stay on sale for seven years
rules.window_note: Covers phones and tablets put on the EU market from 20 June 2025 onwards. Parts have to stay available for at least 7 years after that model stops being sold, and be delivered within 5 to 10 working days. Batteries, screens, front and rear cameras, charging ports, audio sockets, speakers, microphones, buttons, back covers and hinges have to be available to buy, with indicative prices published on a free website. Check the maker's free-access website — they are required to publish the spare parts list, how to order, and indicative prices.
rules.what_you_get: The spare part you need to keep the phone alive instead of binning it. Some parts must be sold to any owner; a longer list of 15 parts must be sold to repair shops. Makers also have to provide at least 5 years of operating system updates, and batteries must still hold 80% of their charge after 800 full charge cycles.
rules.how_to_claim: Ask the maker's support or their parts store for the part by name. If they claim it's discontinued and the model went off sale less than seven years ago, name the ecodesign rules and escalate to your country's market surveillance authority or your European Consumer Centre.
rules.script_hint: Regulation (EU) 2023/1670 requires you to keep spare parts for this model available for at least seven years after end of sales and to deliver them within 5 to 10 working days. Please tell me how to order the part.

rules.title: Anker chargers, cables and power banks are covered for 18 months
rules.window_note: Most Anker gear is covered for 18 months from the day you bought it. Some newer premium lines (Prime, GaNPrime, Nano, MagGo) get 24 months, the PowerCore Reserve power bank gets 36 months, and a few cables are covered for life. That is longer than the 1 year most people assume.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair, a free replacement, or your money back if the charger, cable, power bank, hub or adapter stops working properly on its own.
rules.how_to_claim: Email support@anker.com or call Anker. Have your order number or receipt ready and tell them what the product does wrong.
rules.script_hint: My Anker [product] stopped working on its own and it is still inside the 18-month warranty. I would like a replacement.

rules.title: JBL headphones and speakers: 1 year of free repair or replacement
rules.window_note: One year from the day the product was delivered to you. Bought from a seller JBL approves of, and used in the US.
rules.what_you_get: JBL repairs it or replaces it for free (parts and labour). Sometimes they refund part of what you paid instead. If your product is more than 6 months old, the replacement they send may be a refurbished one.
rules.how_to_claim: Get your receipt or order number, then fill in JBL's warranty exchange form on their support site, or call them.
rules.script_hint: My JBL [product] is faulty and it is under a year old, so it is still in the 1-year warranty. I want it replaced.

rules.title: JBL speakers with no plug get 5 years, not 1
rules.window_note: Five years from delivery. This is for speakers that do not plug into power themselves - the ones you wire to an amplifier or receiver. Almost nobody knows this is five times longer than JBL's normal warranty.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement of the speaker, parts and labour included.
rules.how_to_claim: Find your receipt, then fill in JBL's warranty exchange form or call them, and say the speaker is a non-powered model.
rules.script_hint: This is a non-powered JBL speaker, so it has the 5-year warranty, not the 1-year one. I bought it [date] and it is faulty.

rules.title: Sonos speakers are covered for 1 year
rules.window_note: One year from the day you bought it.
rules.what_you_get: Sonos fixes or replaces the speaker for free if it has a fault in its parts or how it was built.
rules.how_to_claim: Contact Sonos support through their website, tell them your product and what it does, and have your purchase date ready.
rules.script_hint: My Sonos [product] has a fault and I bought it on [date], so it is still in the 1-year warranty.

rules.title: Sonos quietly added a free extra year to speakers bought before Oct 2024
rules.window_note: Sonos added one free extra year on top of the normal warranty. It covers the Arc, Beam, Ray, Five, One, One SL, Era 300, Era 100, Sub, Sub Mini, Port and Amp bought before 1 October 2024. It does not cover portable or wearable Sonos products. So a covered speaker gets 2 years instead of 1 - but the last of these run out on 1 October 2026.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement in year two, when you would normally have been told you were out of warranty.
rules.how_to_claim: Contact Sonos support and point them at their own warranty extension notice, then give them your model and purchase date.
rules.script_hint: My [model] is covered by the Sonos warranty extension announced for 1 October 2024, so I have two years, not one.

rules.title: Jabra earbuds and headsets: 1 year standard
rules.window_note: One year from the date you bought it. This also covers Jabra Elite replacement earbuds, charging pads and charging cases.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement for a faulty product.
rules.how_to_claim: Go back to the shop you bought it from, or contact Jabra support. Bring the product, your receipt, and a short reason for the return.
rules.script_hint: My Jabra [product] is faulty and it is inside the 1-year warranty. Here is my receipt.

rules.title: Jabra gives 2 years against sweat and water damage if you registered the app
rules.window_note: Two years from purchase, running alongside the normal 1-year warranty. You must have registered the earbuds in Jabra's free Sound+ app. This is the rule that saves gym and running earbuds that died from sweat - normally the kind of thing warranties refuse.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement when the earbuds fail because of everyday dust, sweat, rain or splashes.
rules.how_to_claim: Make sure the earbuds are registered in the Jabra Sound+ app, then contact Jabra or your seller and say the failure was caused by sweat or water.
rules.script_hint: These are registered in Sound+, so I am claiming under the 2-year dust and water resistance warranty, not the 1-year one.

rules.title: Beats headphones get Apple's 1-year warranty
rules.window_note: One year from the day you bought them. The cable and other bits in the box are covered too.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement for a manufacturing fault. Apple will post you a prepaid box to send them in, or you can walk into an Apple Store.
rules.how_to_claim: Start a repair on Apple's Beats service page, or book a Genius Bar appointment. No appointment is needed for the mail-in option.
rules.script_hint: My Beats [model] have a manufacturing fault and are under a year old, so they are covered by the Apple Limited Warranty.

rules.title: Razer mice, keyboards and headsets get 2 years, not 1
rules.window_note: Two years from purchase for Razer mice, keyboards, keypads and headsets or earbuds. A few go further: the Viper Mini Signature Edition mouse gets 3 years and the Huntsman Signature Edition keyboard gets 5. Things bought before 1 October 2018 only got 1 year.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement. This is the rule for a mouse that started double-clicking on its own or a keyboard key that stopped registering.
rules.how_to_claim: Open a support case on Razer's support site with your serial number and proof of purchase, and describe the fault.
rules.script_hint: Razer mice and keyboards have a 2-year warranty, not 1 year. Mine was bought [date] and it is faulty.

rules.title: Razer laptop batteries are covered for 2 years even though the laptop is 1
rules.window_note: Razer laptops from 2022 onwards get 1 year on the laptop itself but 2 years on the battery. So a swollen or dead battery in year two is still Razer's problem.
rules.what_you_get: A free battery repair or replacement in the second year, when you would otherwise be told the laptop is out of warranty.
rules.how_to_claim: Open a support case with Razer, give your serial number, and say clearly that this is a battery claim under the separate 2-year battery warranty.
rules.script_hint: This is a battery fault. Razer laptops from 2022 on have a 2-year battery warranty separate from the 1-year laptop warranty.

rules.title: Framework laptops and every part or module: 1 year
rules.window_note: One year from the day the item was delivered. It covers Framework parts and modules on their own, not just whole laptops.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair, replacement or refund. Framework will often just post you the replacement part plus a guide so you can swap it yourself, which is faster than sending the laptop away.
rules.how_to_claim: Email support@frame.work, say which part is faulty and what it does. If the whole laptop has to go back, they send a prepaid shipping label.
rules.script_hint: My Framework [part or laptop] is faulty and it is inside the 1-year warranty. Can you send the replacement part?

rules.title: Lenovo batteries and pens are always capped at 12 months
rules.window_note: Your Lenovo laptop may have a 1, 2 or 3-year warranty depending on the model, but batteries, styluses and digitiser pens are limited to 12 months no matter what the laptop has. Worth checking your exact end date with your serial number - a lot of Lenovo machines are covered for longer than their owners think.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement battery or pen inside the first year. For the laptop itself, a free repair for as long as your base warranty runs.
rules.how_to_claim: Look up your serial number on Lenovo's warranty page to see your real end date, then open a service request.
rules.script_hint: I looked up my serial number and my Lenovo is still in its base warranty. I need a repair booked.

rules.title: HP laptops and printers: 1 year, but check your serial - some have 3
rules.window_note: HP's standard warranty runs 1 to 3 years depending on what you bought. Most consumer laptops get 1 year. Because it varies, the only way to know is to type your serial number into HP's warranty checker - people write off machines that are still covered.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair for faults in the parts or the way it was built.
rules.how_to_claim: Find the serial number (bottom of a laptop, or inside the ink cartridge door on a printer), check it on HP's warranty page, then book the repair.
rules.script_hint: I checked my serial number on your warranty page and it says I am still covered. I would like to book a repair.

rules.title: ASUS laptops include a free year of accidental damage cover
rules.window_note: One year from purchase, on most ASUS laptops and portable displays. This is the big one people miss: normal warranties refuse damage you caused, and this one does not.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair for accidental damage - drops, spills, that kind of thing - which every other laptop maker would charge you for. You did not have to buy anything extra; it comes with the laptop.
rules.how_to_claim: Contact ASUS support and say you are claiming under ASUS Accidental Damage Protection, not the standard warranty. Have your serial number and purchase date.
rules.script_hint: I dropped my ASUS laptop. It is under a year old, so I am claiming under the free Accidental Damage Protection that came with it.

rules.title: One bright stuck pixel gets you a whole new Dell monitor
rules.window_note: It lasts as long as your warranty does - 1 or 3 years for most Dell monitors, or longer if you bought an extended one. Monitors bought together with a computer follow the computer's warranty.
rules.what_you_get: A replacement display. On eligible Dell screens the rule is zero tolerance: even a single bright stuck pixel, or one bright sub-pixel, gets the whole panel swapped. Dark pixels are treated differently - up to about five are allowed.
rules.how_to_claim: Check your service tag is in warranty, then contact Dell support and ask specifically for Premium Panel Exchange. Photograph the bright pixel on a dark screen.
rules.script_hint: My Dell monitor has a bright stuck pixel. Premium Panel Exchange is zero tolerance for bright pixels, so I would like the panel replaced.

rules.title: TCL TVs come with 2 years of parts and labour, not 1
rules.window_note: Two years from purchase or delivery for a TV in a home. Only six months if the TV is used in a business. TCL's warranty statement lists the exact models it covers, so check yours is on the list.
rules.what_you_get: TCL pays for both the parts and the repair work, or swaps the TV for a new or refurbished one. TVs 44 inches and bigger can be repaired or swapped at your home. TCL pays return shipping inside the US.
rules.how_to_claim: Have the model number, serial number and ZIP code ready, plus your receipt, then contact TCL customer support through their support site.
rules.script_hint: TCL TVs have a 2-year parts and labour warranty for home use. Mine was bought [date] and the picture has failed.

rules.title: VIZIO: 1 year, plus a zero bright pixel promise on some screens
rules.window_note: One year from the date you bought it, for home use, from a seller VIZIO approves of in the US, Puerto Rico or Canada.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement with no charge for parts or labour. Some VIZIO screens also carry a Zero Bright Pixel Defect Guarantee, which means a single bright stuck pixel is enough to get the screen replaced. Check the box or the product page to see if yours has it.
rules.how_to_claim: Call VIZIO customer support with your model number and purchase date. Ask directly whether your model has the Zero Bright Pixel guarantee.
rules.script_hint: My VIZIO is under a year old and faulty. Does my model have the Zero Bright Pixel Defect Guarantee?

rules.title: Roku players and remotes: 1 year
rules.window_note: One year from the day you bought the device.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement for hardware that fails during normal use.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to Roku's contact page and pick the Return or Replace option to get a return number before you send anything back.
rules.script_hint: My Roku device is under a year old and has stopped working. I need a return number for a warranty replacement.

rules.title: Every Motorola phone comes with 1 year of free repairs
rules.window_note: One year from purchase, on every Motorola smartphone.
rules.what_you_get: Most repairs cost you nothing inside that year. Cracked screens, other physical damage and water damage are not included - those only get covered if you bought a MotoCare plan.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to Motorola's support site, sign in, enter your phone's IMEI number and describe the problem. They show you the repair options and you start the order online.
rules.script_hint: My Motorola phone is under a year old and failed on its own, so it is covered by the standard 1-year warranty.

rules.title: Canon cameras, lenses and printers: 1 year
rules.window_note: One year across Canon's US range - EOS cameras, PowerShot cameras, lenses, printers and scanners. Refurbished Canon products bought from Canon also get a full year.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement for a fault in the parts or the way it was built.
rules.how_to_claim: Find your model on Canon USA's warranty page, download the warranty sheet for your product type, then contact Canon support with your receipt.
rules.script_hint: My Canon [product] developed a fault and is under a year old, so it is inside the 1-year Canon USA warranty.

rules.title: DJI drones, gimbals, batteries and controllers: 12 months
rules.window_note: Twelve months, counted from the day after your drone was delivered. Batteries also have a charge-cycle limit, so heavy use can end that part of the cover early.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement of the faulty part - the aircraft body, the gimbal and camera, the battery or the remote controller.
rules.how_to_claim: Open a support request on DJI's service site with your serial number, purchase date and a description or video of the fault.
rules.script_hint: My DJI [product] failed on its own within 12 months of delivery, so it is inside the standard warranty.

rules.title: Nintendo consoles, controllers and adapters: 12 months
rules.window_note: Twelve months from the day you bought it, in the US and Canada. It covers the console, game cards, and accessories like controllers and power adapters. If it was a pre-order, the clock starts when it actually arrived.
rules.what_you_get: Nintendo replaces the faulty product free of charge. The replacement may be refurbished, but it has to work like a new one.
rules.how_to_claim: Call Nintendo's consumer assistance line or start a repair on their support site. Do not post anything to Nintendo before contacting them - they will tell you what to send.
rules.script_hint: My Nintendo [product] is faulty and I bought it on [date], so it is inside the 12-month warranty.

rules.title: Drifting Joy-Cons are repaired free forever in the UK and Europe
rules.window_note: There is no time limit. Nintendo says this applies even after the 24-month warranty has run out, and even when the drifting was caused by ordinary wear and tear. It covers Joy-Cons bought in the UK, the European Economic Area and Switzerland. Don't open the controller yourself or use non-Nintendo parts - that voids the free repair. They can still refuse if the damage came from a drop, a third party accessory, or commercial use. With Nintendo covering the postage.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair at an official Nintendo repair centre when the control stick moves your character on its own, or stops responding properly. No charge at all, however old the controller is.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to Nintendo's Joy-Con repair page, try their troubleshooting steps, then book a repair using the form on that page.
rules.script_hint: My Joy-Con stick is drifting. Nintendo repairs this free of charge in the UK and EEA even after the warranty has expired.

rules.title: PlayStation 5 consoles: 1 year
rules.window_note: One year from the original purchase date, in the US and Canada. Registering the console makes no difference - you get the same cover either way. This covers the console itself; controllers and other accessories are handled separately.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair, or a replacement console that has been factory-recertified.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to playstation.com/repairs to get a return authorisation and shipping instructions. You need a dated receipt showing where and when you bought it.
rules.script_hint: My PS5 is under a year old and faulty. I need a return authorisation for warranty service.

rules.title: Steam Deck and Valve Index: 1 year, prepaid label included
rules.window_note: One year from the day it shipped to you. If you live in the EU, the UK, Quebec, Australia or New Zealand this warranty does not apply to you at all - your country's own consumer law covers you instead, which is usually better. Scratches and marks from ordinary use do not void it.
rules.what_you_get: Valve repairs it, replaces it with a new or refurbished one, or refunds what you paid. In the US they send you a prepaid shipping label, so posting it back costs you nothing.
rules.how_to_claim: Submit a help request at help.steampowered.com before sending anything. They will give you a return number and, in the US, a prepaid label.
rules.script_hint: My Steam Deck is faulty and shipped less than a year ago. I would like to start a warranty return.

rules.title: LG fridge: the whole cooling system is covered for 5 years
rules.window_note: Five years from the purchase date. This is separate from the 1-year warranty on everything else.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair with no bill at all: LG covers both the parts and the repair person's time for 5 years on the sealed cooling system. That means the condenser, the evaporator, the drier and the pipes that connect them.
rules.how_to_claim: If your fridge is warm, frosting over oddly, or running constantly, book an LG service call and ask them to check the sealed system. Say up front that you believe it is a sealed-system fault so it gets logged as warranty work.
rules.script_hint: My LG fridge isn't cooling properly. Sealed system parts and labour are covered for 5 years, and mine is inside that window, so please book this as a warranty repair.

rules.title: Samsung fridge: 10 years on the compressor, 5 on the cooling system
rules.window_note: Ten years from purchase for the compressor part. The sealed cooling system gets 5 years of parts and labour. Everything else is 1 year. Check your own model, as terms can differ. The repair has to be done by a Samsung authorised service centre to stay free.
rules.what_you_get: A free digital inverter compressor for 10 years. Samsung also covers the repair person's time on the sealed system for 5 years, so inside 5 years a cooling failure should cost you nothing.
rules.how_to_claim: Call Samsung or start a service request online with your model and serial number (sticker inside the fridge). Tell them the fridge is not cooling and ask them to check the compressor and sealed system under the extended warranty.
rules.script_hint: My Samsung fridge has stopped cooling. The digital inverter compressor has a 10-year parts warranty and the sealed system has 5 years of parts and labour. Please book this as a warranty repair.

rules.title: Samsung washer: 10 years on the motor if you bought it April 2026 or later
rules.window_note: Ten years from purchase, but only for washers bought on 1 April 2026 or later. Older Samsung washers do not get this. The rest of the machine is covered for 1 year.
rules.what_you_get: A free digital inverter motor for 10 years. A motor is one of the most expensive parts of a washing machine, and a dead motor is the usual reason people bin an otherwise fine washer.
rules.how_to_claim: Dig out your receipt first, because Samsung requires proof of the purchase date for this one. Then call Samsung or book service online and tell them the motor has failed.
rules.script_hint: My Samsung washer's motor has failed. I bought it after 1 April 2026, so the digital inverter motor is covered for 10 years. I have my receipt showing the purchase date.

rules.title: Samsung washer or dryer: 10 years on the inverter motor
rules.window_note: Samsung's appliance warranty page lists 1 year parts and labour overall, plus 10-year cover on the digital inverter motor in washers and dryers. Check your own model to be sure yours has that motor.
rules.what_you_get: If the drum motor fails, Samsung covers the motor for 10 years from purchase instead of the usual 1 year.
rules.how_to_claim: Note the model and serial number from the door frame or back panel, then book a repair with Samsung and say you are claiming on the 10-year digital inverter motor cover.
rules.script_hint: The motor in my Samsung washer has failed and you cover the digital inverter motor for 10 years - please book this as a warranty repair.

rules.title: Sub-Zero fridge: cooling parts covered for 12 years
rules.window_note: Counted from when the fridge was installed, not when it was bought. Twelve years for the cooling parts, 5 years for those same parts with the labour included, and 2 years for the whole appliance.
rules.what_you_get: Three layers of cover. Years 1-2: everything on the fridge, parts and labour, free. Years 1-5: the compressor, condenser, evaporator, drier and connecting pipes, parts and labour, free. Years 6-12: those same cooling parts still free, but you pay the repair person's time.
rules.how_to_claim: Call Sub-Zero and ask for the Factory Certified Service company nearest you. Use their approved service company, because if you use an outside repairer Sub-Zero will only send you the part and will not pay you back for parts you bought elsewhere. Note that fan motors are not part of the cooling system and are not covered by the 12-year rule.
rules.script_hint: My Sub-Zero was installed less than 12 years ago and the sealed system has failed. That's covered for 12 years on parts. Please send Factory Certified Service and supply the part under warranty.

rules.title: Bosch dishwasher: control board and racks covered to year 5
rules.window_note: Years 2 through 5 after you bought it. Year 1 is full cover including labour, so this rule matters most once that first year has run out.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement circuit board or dish rack. Bosch covers the electronics (the microprocessor or printed circuit board) and the racks for parts right through to the end of year 5. You pay the repair person's time.
rules.how_to_claim: A dead control panel, buttons that do nothing, or a machine that will not start is usually the circuit board. Rusted or collapsing racks count too, though the small clips and tines on the racks are not included. Call Bosch with your model and serial number.
rules.script_hint: My Bosch dishwasher's control board has failed and the machine is under 5 years old. Bosch covers the electronics for parts from year 2 through year 5, so I'd like the part supplied under warranty.

rules.title: Bosch vacuum: register it and the motor is covered for 10 years
rules.window_note: Ten years from purchase, but only if you registered the vacuum with Bosch. The vacuum itself is covered for 2 years or 300 hours of use, whichever comes first.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement motor for 10 years. This is the single most valuable part in a vacuum, and it only applies if you registered the machine, so it is worth registering today even if nothing is wrong yet.
rules.how_to_claim: First check whether you ever registered it. If not, register it now so future you is covered. If the motor has already died and you did register, call Bosch's vacuum and espresso line rather than the main appliance line.
rules.script_hint: My registered Bosch vacuum's motor has failed. Registered Bosch vacuums have a 10-year parts warranty on the motor, so I'd like a replacement motor supplied under that warranty.

rules.title: Bosch built-in fridge: extra cover most owners never hear about
rules.window_note: Year 1 is everything, parts and labour. Year 2 is every part, free. Years 3 to 5 cover the electronics. Rust-through on the stainless door has no time limit at all.
rules.what_you_get: Free parts for the whole fridge right through year 2, free circuit boards through year 5, and a free stainless steel door for life if it rusts through. This only applies to built-in models, not freestanding ones.
rules.how_to_claim: Check whether yours is a built-in model (it slots into the cabinetry and takes a cabinet front panel). Call Bosch's large appliance line with your model and serial number and name which of these tiers you are claiming under.
rules.script_hint: I have a Bosch built-in refrigerator that's under 2 years old. Built-in models get parts cover for the entire appliance through the second year, so please supply this part under warranty.

rules.title: Speed Queen TC5 washer: the gearbox is covered for 15 years
rules.window_note: Fifteen years from installation on the transmission for TC5 models. Years 4 to 15 are parts only, so you pay the repair person's time but not the part.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement transmission (the gearbox that turns the drum) for fifteen years. This is one of the longest single-part warranties on any home appliance and it is almost never mentioned at the point of sale.
rules.how_to_claim: Check whether your model number starts TC5. If the drum will not spin or agitate, or the machine makes a grinding noise under load, ask for the transmission to be checked specifically.
rules.script_hint: My Speed Queen TC5 washer's transmission has failed. The transmission assembly carries a 15-year warranty on that model, so please supply the part under warranty.

rules.title: Speed Queen: the drum and tub are covered for life against rust
rules.window_note: No time limit. This one runs for as long as you own the machine. The cabinet has its own separate 5-year cover against rusting from the inside out.
rules.what_you_get: A free stainless steel wash tub or dryer cylinder if it rusts or corrodes, with no deadline. Speed Queen covers the stainless tub and outer tub on washers, and the steel cylinder and bulkheads on dryers, for life.
rules.how_to_claim: Look for rust streaks on your laundry, rough or flaking metal inside the drum, or brown water. Photograph it. Note that surface rust from something you left in the machine, and rust caused by chemicals, are excluded, so describe it as rust coming from the metal itself.
rules.script_hint: The stainless steel tub in my Speed Queen washer is corroding. Speed Queen gives a lifetime warranty on the stainless tub against rust or corrosion, so I'd like the part replaced under that warranty.

rules.title: Maytag: 10 years of free parts on almost everything they make
rules.window_note: Ten years from purchase, on any major Maytag kitchen or laundry appliance made after 2017. Year 1 includes labour; years 2 to 10 are the part only.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement for the expensive core part of your appliance. On washers and dryers that's the drive motor, wash basket and dryer drum. On dishwashers it's the stainless tub, nylon racks and chopper. On fridges it's the compressor. On microwaves it's the magnetron and cavity. On ranges and ovens it's the burners, elements, ceramic top, grates and cavity.
rules.how_to_claim: Check the appliance was made after 2017 (the serial number sticker gives the build date). Work out which of the listed parts has failed, then call Maytag or book service and name that part. Two specific laundry pairs also get labour covered for the first 5 years, so ask whether yours is one of them.
rules.script_hint: My Maytag was made after 2017 and the drive motor has failed. That part is covered by Maytag's 10-year limited parts warranty, so I'd like the part supplied free.

rules.title: Dyson corded vacuum: 5 years, parts and labour
rules.window_note: Five years from purchase or delivery, whichever is later. If you have lost your receipt, Dyson starts the clock 90 days after the machine was made, so you may still have time.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair covering both parts and labour for five years on upright and canister vacuums (and Dyson lights and hand dryers). Registering is not required and does not change your rights.
rules.how_to_claim: Call the Dyson helpline with your model name, serial number and where and when you bought it. Note that blockages, worn filters, worn brush bars and a battery simply getting older are not covered, so describe an actual fault rather than a maintenance issue.
rules.script_hint: My Dyson corded vacuum has developed a fault. Corded Dyson vacuums carry a 5-year parts and labour warranty and mine is inside that window, so I'd like it repaired at no cost.

rules.title: Roomba: the battery is inside the 1-year warranty
rules.window_note: One year from purchase, or from delivery if that was later. If the delivery date can't be checked, the clock starts two weeks after purchase.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement robot. The battery and the Clean Base dirt-disposal unit both count as part of the robot, so a battery that has actually failed is covered, not just the robot body.
rules.how_to_claim: Have your serial number and your receipt from an approved seller ready before you contact iRobot. You do not need to have registered the robot: iRobot states in writing that not registering does not reduce your rights. Note that a battery just getting weaker with age counts as wear and is not covered, and robots bought from unapproved sellers are not covered at all.
rules.script_hint: My Roomba is under a year old and has failed. iRobot's warranty covers the robot including the battery for one year, so I'd like it repaired or replaced.

rules.title: Miele vacuum: the motor and body are covered for 7 years
rules.window_note: Seven years from purchase, but only on the S-series machines: model numbers starting S2, S4, S5, S6, S7, S8, S160 or S190. Everything else on those vacuums is only covered for 1 year, which is why owners assume the whole machine is out of warranty.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair, parts and labour, if the suction motor or the power head motor dies, or if the plastic body cracks or breaks. On the S8990 model these go to 10 years instead of 7.
rules.how_to_claim: Check your model number on the underside or back of the vacuum. If it starts with one of those S codes and the motor has gone, contact Miele or an approved Miele dealer. This is a US-only warranty and does not apply to vacuums used for work.
rules.script_hint: My Miele S-series vacuum's motor has failed. Miele covers vacuum and power head motors for 7 years on the S-series, separately from the 1-year warranty on the rest of the machine.

rules.title: Cuisinart: 3 years, and no receipt needed to try
rules.window_note: Three years from purchase on Cuisinart kitchen appliances, which is three times the usual one year. If you cannot find your receipt, Cuisinart uses the date the item was made instead, so a missing receipt does not end the conversation.
